Brings **up to three GCE Electronics IPX800 V4 or V5** into Gladys through
their local HTTP API: their relays, their digital inputs, the pilot-wire
zones of their X-4FP extensions and their X-THL sensors (temperature,
humidity, luminosity).

> Never tested with a real device: written from the GCE documentation of the
> V4 API and from the open-source libraries of the Home Assistant
> integrations (pypx800, pypx800v5). Please report what you see on yours.
> Not affiliated with GCE Electronics.

## Setup

1. In the IPX800, create an **API key**: V5 under System > API, V4 under
   Network > API (tick the API access).
2. In Gladys, Integrations > IPX800: choose the model (V5 or V4), type the
   address of the IPX800 (e.g. `192.168.1.50`, give it a fixed address in
   your router) and the API key. On the same page, list in "Relays Gladys
   may drive" the relays Gladys must drive, and only those (e.g. `R1, R2`;
   see "Relays" below: never a pump, a ventilation, a door strike…). Then
   save.
3. "Test the connection" reads the IPX800 now (once an interval has passed
   since the last read) and shows what it found. An X-8R output (V5) is
   listed by the code in its name in Discover (e.g. `X8R4259840-3`): add it
   to the list now, before creating it.
4. In Discover, create the devices you want. A listed relay comes as a
   switch (or a light); the others come **read only** ("State (read
   only)"): Gladys shows their state, nothing can switch them.

A relay listed **after** its creation stays read only until you click
**"Update"** on it in Discover: it then gets its switch (or light), next to
its "State (read only)", which stays. The status of the integration says
how many relays are read only while none is listed, and which listed relays
still wait for "Update".

The IPX800 wants the API key in the address of every request, over plain
http: anyone who can watch your local network can read it, as with the
IPX800's own apps. The key is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown
again, sent only to the IPX800, and never written in the logs nor in the
files of the integration.

The model chosen must be the IPX800's: a V4 chosen as "V5" (or the reverse)
is recognized, the status and "Test the connection" say so ("This IPX800 is
a V4, but "Model" says V5"), and nothing is read nor sent until the model is
fixed.

## Several IPX800

A V5 and a V4 in the same house (or two V5): keep the first one in the
fields at the top, and put the other one in **"IPX800 #2"** (model, address
with `:port` if needed, API key, its relays Gladys may drive, its V4
extensions), a third one in "IPX800 #3". Each has its own devices in
Discover ("IPX800 #2 · Relay 1 (R1)"), its own list of relays to drive and
its own part of the status (one block, the IPX800 separated by " | "). The
poll interval, the heating option and the language are shared.

**Do not change the slot of an IPX800 to try another one**: the devices
already created stay with their slot. To go from a V5 to a V4, add the V4
as #2 instead of replacing the V5.

## Each IPX800 keeps its devices

A device created for one IPX800 does not drive another one, even when you
change the address, the port or the model of its slot (three limits:
another V4 put at the same address, see "Limits"; the devices of 0.1.2, see
below; and devices whose IPX800 is not known, whose Off and Frost protection
go to the address typed, see below). The integration keeps in `/data`
which IPX800 the devices of each slot belong to: a **V5 by its MAC
address** (read again at every read, kept as a salted fingerprint), a **V4
by its address and port** (its API gives no MAC address).

When the IPX800 read is not theirs (another MAC address, another model, a V4
at another address), then:

- no command leaves for it, not even an Off;
- the Offs kept for the old one are dropped;
- none of its values is published onto these devices;
- the Discover list is empty for that slot;
- the status says so.

Then put back the model and the address of their IPX800. If you **replaced**
it, changed the address of a V4, or when the status asks for it for devices
of 0.1.2, click **"Attach the devices" twice** (within a minute), choosing
the slot: its devices then drive the IPX800 read, with the relays listed for
that slot. A slot without any device created simply takes the IPX800 it
reads. When the MAC address of a V5 can no longer be read (after a firmware
update, say), "Attach the devices" knows it by its address, as a V4.

One IPX800 goes in one slot only. When two slots hold the same address, the
one whose devices' IPX800 was checked at that address keeps it (otherwise
the first one); the other is not read, nothing is sent to its devices, not
even an Off, and its status says which address to correct.

When the IPX800 of the devices is **not known** (`/data` emptied or deleted,
Gladys restored on another machine: its backups do not hold the `/data` of
the integrations; `/data` that cannot be read, or written while it holds
nothing yet), nothing proves another IPX800 at the address typed: Off and
Frost protection go there, as do the resends of an Off the reads do not
show. Switching on, the heating modes and the values wait for "Attach the
devices" (two clicks), and the status says so.

When the MAC address of a V5 cannot be read, only Off and Frost protection
leave, and only to the address it was last checked at. When a V5 starts, and
after a failed read, its MAC address is read again before anything is sent:
the Offs kept leave after that check, and an Off clicked waits for it 1.5 s
at most, then leaves for the address it was last checked at.

**Coming from 0.1.2**: 0.1.2 kept only the last IPX800 it read, not the one
the devices were created for. **Before updating, put back in the top fields
the IPX800 you created the devices for.** After the update, the devices
already created are "to be confirmed": only Off and Frost protection are
sent to them, and only to the address 0.1.2 read (another address typed:
nothing at all until "Attach the devices"). The status names the
IPX800 read (model, MAC address or address) and the number of devices. If
they are its own, click "Attach the devices" twice: everything works again.
If not, put their IPX800 back in the top fields, and the other one in a slot
of its own. When they hold codes that model does not have (an X-4FP zone of
a V5 with "V4" chosen, say), nothing is sent to them, not even an Off.

## What you get

| On the IPX800                   | In Gladys                                                                | Code (in the name)         |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| Relay (V4 1-56, V5 1-8)         | read only, or a switch / light if you list it                            | `R3`                       |
| X-8R output (V5)                | the same                                                                 | `X8R4259840-3` (its id)    |
| Digital input (V4 1-56, V5 1-8) | a binary input (read only)                                               | `D3`                       |
| X-8D / X-24D input (V5)         | the same                                                                 | `X8D5-2`, `X24D6-10`       |
| X-4FP zone                      | pilot wire (Off, Frost protection, Eco, Comfort, Comfort -1, Comfort -2) | `FP5` (V4), `X4FP7-2` (V5) |
| X-THL                           | temperature (°C), humidity (%), luminosity (lux)                         | `THL1` (V4), `XTHL9` (V5)  |

**V5**: the integration lists the extensions itself. **V4**: the API answers
56 relays and 56 inputs whether they are wired or not; the integration shows
the 8 relays and 8 inputs of the IPX, and what you list in "Extensions of an
IPX800 V4", e.g. `R9-R16, D9-D16, FP1-FP4, THL1` (pilot-wire zone n of the
V4 is zone z of X-4FP e: n = 4 × (e − 1) + z).

The IPX800 is read every 10 seconds by default (5 s at least). A value the
IPX800 does not give (absent, a text, out of range) is not published: never
as 0.
On the V5, an X-THL whose own "measurement fault" IO is on publishes
nothing until it clears, and the status names it; Gladys keeps showing its
last published value. The ids of the V5 extensions are those the IPX800
gives them (often 7 digits): copy the code from the device name.

## Relays: read only unless you list them

A relay you do not list is **read only**. To drive one from Gladys, list it
in "Relays Gladys may drive", e.g. `R1, R3:light, X8R4259840-2` (`:light`
makes it a light, otherwise a switch), preferably before creating it in
Discover; already created, click "Update" on it in Discover. A switch or a light obeys every "turn everything
off" of Google, Alexa, the MCP and the scenes: never list a pump, a freezer,
a ventilation, a heating, a door strike nor a valve. A relay you remove from
the list is read only again at once: its commands are refused, and a
switch-off the integration was still holding for it is dropped (in memory
and in `/data`, also at a restart). Its switch stays on the device in Gladys
(without effect): Gladys does not delete one feature alone; only deleting
the device, then creating it again, removes it, with its history.

## Pilot wire

- **Off** and **Frost protection** need no option and go before everything
  else: during a pause after failed reads, with a refused API key, with the
  queue of commands full, and before the first read after a restart (the V5
  ids are kept in `/data`). Clicked, they interrupt any request in progress
  (a read, a read back, a command, a resend), except another Off or Frost
  protection clicked just before. The same goes for switching off a relay
  you listed.
- **Eco, Comfort, Comfort -1, Comfort -2** drive the heating: they are off by
  default. Tick "Allow Eco and Comfort from Gladys" to allow them; every
  Gladys user, every scene and the Gladys app can then choose them. They are
  refused while the state cannot be written to `/data`.

An Off or Frost protection is refused only when: the address or the API key
is missing or not valid, or the slot has the address of another slot that
keeps it; the zone is not known (V4: not listed in the extensions; V5: never
read: its ids are kept in `/data` and across a new session, and without them
an Off waits 2.5 s at most for the first read); the value is not one of the
six modes; the IPX800 read is proven not to be the device's (another MAC
address, another model, a V4 at another address, devices of 0.1.2 holding
codes the model chosen cannot have, devices of 0.1.2 with another address
than 0.1.2's typed); while the MAC address of a V5 is read or cannot be
read, at another address than the one it was last checked at (see "Each
IPX800 keeps its devices"). An unknown owner is no refusal: the Off goes to
the address typed.
Off for a relay is refused when the relay is not listed. Clicked before the
configuration is read from Gladys (the API key is kept there only, never in
`/data`), it asks Gladys for it at once and waits 3 s; if it has not come,
it is kept in memory and sent as soon as the API key is known (read again
5 s later, then every minute at most), before anything is sent to Gladys;
if the output turns out unknown or not listed, the status says so. An Off
kept in `/data` leaves the same way at start, without waiting for Gladys.
When the IPX800 does not take it within 3.5 s (no connection), it is kept
and sent again as soon as the IPX800 is free, before the read backs, by the
next reads that show another mode, and after a restart. An Off clicked while
another one gets no answer for 1 s interrupts it. A resend interrupted by a
click before it left goes again right behind that click.

An Off or Frost protection that the reads do not show is sent again, 3 times
at most; then the status says so (check on site). A V5 zone with several
modes on is shown as such in the status and gets the Off again. It stays
held until a later command on that zone leaves (your click), another Off /
Frost protection, or, once applied, another mode read twice in a row
(changed on the IPX800 itself, by its scenarios or its page): never by the
time. Anything asked before an Off on the same zone and not yet sent is
cancelled, a Frost protection waiting to be tried again included: it never
leaves after it. A mode the integration sent before the Off and that got no
answer (cut by the Off, say), if the IPX800 still applies it in the 5 s
after it left, is not a change on the IPX800: the Off is sent again.

`/data` (the state of the integration) is read and written within 1.5 s or
treated as unreadable or not written: a disk that does not answer never
stops the reads, the status, "Test the connection" nor an Off. One read and
one save at a time: a save that does not end is not piled on (the status
says `/data` cannot be written, heating modes and "Attach the devices" are
refused), and the state of now is written once it ends. The Offs held and
the V5 ids survive a new session (a new API key) in memory.

## Commands

A command is written within 3.5 s of the click or refused with "nothing was
sent". It is then read back from the IPX800: the value asked is a success;
another value is "not applied yet"; no answer in time is "sent, without
confirmation". Two more reads follow after 5 s and 20 s. The commands of a
scene are written one after the other, then read back once.

## Pauses and refusals

A failed read pauses 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min then 5 min (one minute at
least when the IPX800 answers 429 or 503), kept across restarts; Eco,
Comfort and switching a relay on are refused until the pause ends. An API key
refused by the IPX800 (401, 403) stops the reads until you change the key or
"Test the connection" succeeds. While an IPX800 does not answer (or refuses
the key, or is not of the model chosen), its devices leave the Discover list;
a Scan does not bring them back. They come back at the first good read.

## Limits

- X-8R, X-8D, X-24D, X-4FP and X-THL only; counters, X-4VR shutters,
  dimmers, X-PWM, virtual inputs and outputs are not in this version.
- Three IPX800 at most per integration.
- A V4 is known by its address: after a change of address, "Attach the
  devices" (two clicks) is needed; and another V4 put at the same address
  cannot be told apart (the V4 API gives no MAC address).
- http only (the IPX800 answers http on the local network).

## So installierst du IPX800 in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: IPX800 erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-ipx800:0.1.3`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ipx800](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ipx800).

IPX800 benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

IPX800 ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.

- [Alle Integrationen durchsuchen](/de/docs/integrations/), native und aus der Community
